facts.title: A 9,500-Year-Old Grave in Cyprus Holds a Person Buried With a Cat
facts.summary: At Shillourokambos, a Neolithic village on the island of Cyprus, archaeologists found a person and a cat buried together in a grave about 9,500 years old.

facts.title: A Cat's Larynx Can Purr Even Without Signals From the Brain
facts.summary: For about 50 years, scientists believed a cat could only purr if its brain sent a steady rhythm of signals making the voice box muscles twitch.

facts.title: Blotched Tabby Cats Only Became Common in the Middle Ages
facts.summary: The swirling, blotched tabby coat seen on many house cats today is a fairly recent fashion.

facts.title: Cats Can See in Light Only 16 Percent as Bright as Humans Need
facts.summary: Domestic cats can see in conditions only about 16 percent as bright as the light people need to see, thanks to a mirror-like layer at the back of their eyes.

facts.title: Cats Hide a Cry Inside Their Purr When They Want to Be Fed
facts.summary: Some cats have a special purr for breakfast time.

facts.title: Cats Rolling in Silver Vine and Catnip Gain Protection From Mosquitoes
facts.summary: The famous catnip frenzy may be more than a high.

facts.title: China's First Village Cats Were Leopard Cats, Not Ancestors of Today's Pets
facts.summary: About 5,300 years ago, cats lived alongside farmers in central China, but they were not the ancestors of modern pets.

facts.title: Domestic Cats' Meows Sound More Pleasant to People Than Wildcat Calls
facts.summary: House cats seem to have developed meows that people find pleasant.

facts.title: Every House Cat Descends From the Near Eastern Wildcat
facts.summary: A genetic study of 979 cats found that the world's house cats, whether pampered pets or strays, all trace back to one wild ancestor: the Near Eastern wildcat, Felis silvestris lybica.

facts.title: Félicette, a Small Tuxedo Cat, Became the First Cat in Space in 1963
facts.summary: On 18 October 1963, a small black and white cat named Félicette rode a French rocket to the edge of space and came back alive, becoming the first cat in space.

facts.title: Female Cats Tend to Be Right-Pawed While Males Favour the Left
facts.summary: Cats have a dominant paw, and which one it is depends largely on sex.

facts.title: Feral Cats Are Linked to 63 Extinctions of Birds, Mammals and Reptiles
facts.summary: Domestic cats gone wild have helped drive 63 species of birds, mammals and reptiles to extinction, according to a 2016 global review.

facts.title: House Cats Can Tell Their Own Names Apart From Other Words
facts.summary: Cats may act aloof, but experiments in Japan show that many can pick out their own name from a list of similar-sounding words.

facts.title: Only About 1 in 3,000 Calico Cats Is Male
facts.summary: Calico and tortoiseshell cats are almost always female.

facts.title: Outdoor Cats Kill Billions of Birds in the United States Every Year
facts.summary: Free-ranging cats are one of the largest human-linked causes of bird deaths in the United States.

facts.title: Slow Blinking at a Cat Makes It More Likely to Approach You
facts.summary: Scientists have confirmed that the slow blink works: when people narrow their eyes and slowly blink at a cat, the cat tends to slow blink back and becomes more willing to approach.

facts.title: Tons of Mummified Egyptian Cats Were Shipped to Britain as Fertiliser
facts.summary: In 1890, about 19.5 tons of mummified cats from an ancient Egyptian cemetery near the town of Beni Hasan were shipped to Liverpool, England, where they were crushed and used as fertiliser.
